summary.text: The Monsoon of South Asia is one of the world's monsoons, an economically important pattern over the Indian subcontinent every year from June through September.
Its winds gather moisture over the surrounding seas, then drop heavy rain when highlands such as the Western Ghats and the Himalayas force the air to rise.
It shapes farming and water supply so much that it has been called the "real finance minister of India", yet its rains remain hard to predict.

facts.label: Usual onset
facts.value: Western coast near Thiruvananthapuram, early June

facts.label: Withdrawal
facts.value: Starts early September, ends by early October

items.prompt: Imagine the Himalayas were not there. What would happen to the southwest monsoon winds?

options.label: They would drop even more rain on India
They would stop and turn back out to sea
They would blow on to Tibet and beyond without raining
They would freeze into snow over the plains

items.explain: Without the Himalayas, the southwest monsoon winds would blow over the subcontinent into Tibet, Afghanistan and Russia without causing rain.

items.prompt: Moist sea wind runs into a steep coastal mountain range. Where does most of its rain fall?

options.label: On the slopes facing the wind
On the sheltered far side
Out over the open sea
Evenly across the region

items.explain: Mountains force the wind to rise, and the rising moist air cools and condenses, so rain falls on the windward side.

items.prompt: People in India have nicknamed the monsoon the country's "real finance minister". What does the nickname point to?

options.label: It is forecast by the government
It arrives when budgets are set
It is taxed like a business
Its rains shape people's livelihoods

items.explain: The monsoon affects agriculture and the overall well-being of residents so strongly that it earned this nickname.

items.prompt: Hot, dry weeks end and newspapers announce that the monsoon has "burst". What has happened?

options.label: A dam has broken after heavy rain
Daily rainfall has jumped suddenly
The winds have stopped completely
A cyclone has hit the coast

items.explain: The burst of the monsoon is the sudden change from hot, dry weather to wet, humid weather, with an abrupt rise in mean daily rainfall.

items.prompt: Who were the first people to notice how the monsoon's branches fit together across South Asia?

options.label: Astronomers tracking the stars
Farmers in the Himalayan valleys
Sailors crossing the Arabian Sea
Scientists with weather balloons

items.explain: Sailors in the Arabian Sea travelling between Africa, India and Southeast Asia were the first to observe the combined pattern.

items.prompt: One year India receives its usual total amount of monsoon rain. What can still cause trouble?

options.label: The rain can arrive at the wrong times or places
The rain can turn salty from the nearby sea
The winds can stop reversing for good
The rivers can flow uphill into the hills

items.explain: Even with enough total rain, its timing can be arbitrary and its daily or geographic spread can be badly skewed.
